init.title: MSpa Integration Settings
init.description: Configure the power consumption values for accurate energy monitoring. These values are based on your hot tub model specifications but can be adjusted to match your actual measurements.

data.track_temperature_unit: Reset the spa's °C/°F after a power cut
data.always_enforce_unit: Check the unit on every poll, not only after a power cut
data.restore_state: Restore the previous settings after a power cut
data.schedule_target_temp: Target temperature for a scheduled heat-up

data_description.pump_power: Power consumption when the filter pump is running (typically 60W)
data_description.bubble_power: Power consumption when bubbles are active (typically 900W)
data_description.track_temperature_unit: The spa forgets whether it is set to Celsius or Fahrenheit when it loses power. When it comes back online, set it again to match Home Assistant.
data_description.always_enforce_unit: For spas that forget the unit without ever losing power. Checks on every update and sends a command only when the unit is actually wrong.
data_description.restore_state: When the spa comes back online, send back the target temperature and settings it had before the power cut. This writes to the spa, so leave it off if you would rather nothing were set on your behalf.
data_description.weather_entity: Select a weather entity (e.g. Met.no, OpenWeatherMap) to bias heating estimates by ambient temperature and wind speed. Historical sessions are weighted by how closely their conditions match the current weather.
data_description.schedule_target_temp: What a scheduled heat-up aims for, as opposed to the setpoint you choose by hand. Also adjustable at any time from the Schedule Target Temperature entity.
data_description.outdoor_sensor: A temperature sensor outside, near the spa. Nothing depends on it yet — it is recorded alongside the forecast so the two can be compared over real heat-ups. A forecast describes the region; a thermometer in your garden describes the air the spa is actually losing heat to, and shelter, sun and cold air pooling can separate them by several degrees overnight. On a long heat-up the estimate moves roughly twenty minutes per degree, so it is worth knowing which to trust.

weather_forecast_unavailable.title: MSpa cannot read a weather forecast
weather_forecast_unavailable.description:
MSpa uses the hourly forecast from `{entity_id}` to work out when to start heating for a scheduled ready time, and how long a heat-up under way still needs. Right now it cannot: {detail}.

Heating and scheduling carry on working. Estimates fall back to the current outdoor temperature, and then to the seasonal average this spa has learned its heating rates under, so they stay usable but become less accurate — most noticeably for a long overnight heat-up, where the temperature at the moment of planning describes neither end of the run.

To fix it, check that the weather integration providing `{entity_id}` is working and that the entity offers a forecast. You can also choose a different weather entity, or clear it entirely, in the MSpa options. This notice clears itself once a forecast is readable again.
